summary.headline: CSB Bank FY26 net profit rose 7% to Rs.633 crore; Q4 profit Rs.202 crore (+32% QoQ) with GNPA at a low 1.66%.
summary.overview: CSB Bank closed FY26 with net profit of Rs.633 crore (+7% YoY) and Q4 net profit of Rs.202 crore, up 32% QoQ, with Q4 RoA of 1.53% and RoE of 17.66%. Advances grew 27% and deposits 20% YoY, both ahead of industry, but deposit growth leaned on bulk/wholesale deposits (around 50% of term deposits) and gold loans rose to about 53% of the book. Asset quality improved to GNPA 1.66% and NNPA 0.40%, helped by lower slippages and higher recoveries. Management guided retail asset growth only from FY28, CTI of 60-65% through FY27, and RoA/RoE of about 1.5%/15% next year.

financial_highlights.change: +17% YoY; Q4 NII +25% YoY, about +2% QoQ per analyst calc
+21% YoY; no syndication fee in Q4; PSLC premium very low; treasury gains lower

financial_highlights.value: Rs.272 / Rs.36.5 FY; Q4 EPS Rs.47.12
Average LCR 109% in Q4; NSFR about 122%

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold share of book rose from about 44% to about 53% YoY, partly from reclassification of loan-against-security (LAS) with gold collateral (down from over Rs.2,000 crore to about Rs.300 crore). Account count has fallen (from about 6-7 lakh to 4 lakh over three years) as the bank shifted to larger tickets above Rs.10 lakh.

segments.name: Business Lending Group (SME + LAP)
segments.commentary: BLG grew about 2-3% in FY26 by deliberate choice; SME is about 11% of book versus a 2030 target of about 18%. Management expects single-digit growth for now and a return to 28-30% growth within two years.

segments.name: Retail assets
segments.commentary: Retail assets declined YoY largely due to the gold LAS reclassification; unsecured book shrinking. New products are School Fee Financing and LAS against mutual funds. Meaningful retail asset growth is guided from FY28.

segments.name: Wholesale / corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate portfolio progressing as planned; relationship team expanded from low double digits to 80-plus, and transaction banking (Vayana, Aurion Pro CMS, trade) to go live in 3-4 months.

guidance_outlook: CTI to stay in 60-65% through FY27; operating leverage expected from FY28, with CTI much lower by FY30.
NIM expected in the 3.75-4% range; management says it is not sure NIM has bottomed.
Loan growth targeted around 25% next year, dependent on deposit and CASA build-up; CASA balances to take about one year to grow.
RoA about 1.5% and RoE about 15% expected to sustain next year.
Retail asset growth to start meaningfully from FY28 (Q4 FY27/Q1 FY28 for portfolio growth); gold loans targeted at 30% of book by 2030.
ECL transition impact described as not significant, pending model refresh; ECL transition date April 1, 2027 with four-year capital phase-in.
capex_capacity: Core banking migrated to a new system (rolled out May 2025) with surround systems; management says stabilisation is now complete.
Network of 862 branches and 832 ATMs as of March 31, 2026.
Headcount up about 570 to a base of about 7,600 (under 8%), with cost rising faster as high-cost wholesale talent was hired.
Dubai representative office application extended due to West Asia crisis; CRO appointed.
Transaction banking systems and LMS/LOS, data center investment and OBDX planned over the next few quarters.
demand_pricing: Deposit growth lagged advances; bulk and wholesale deposits about 50% of term deposits and CASA about 20%; wholesale deposits mostly maturing within six months.
Q4 wholesale deposit cost fell more than 30 bps from Q1, and overall deposit cost fell about 10 bps from Q1.
NRI deposits about 13% of deposits; target at least 20% over the long run.
Yield compression came from repo rate cuts through BLG and MCLR repricing in wholesale, which management says has largely played out.
PSLC premium very low in Q4 and treasury/MTM gains absent versus Q4 FY25; core fees (ex-PSLC, ex-treasury) grew.
Gold loans priced higher for larger-ticket customers moving from NBFCs, lifting portfolio yields by around 40 bps over the last 3-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is LCR declining and how will wholesale deposits (about 50% of term deposits) affect growth and cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 average LCR was 109% against a 110% target, a tactical choice to avoid higher March deposit costs; LCR is now well above that. Short-tenor bulk deposits are a tactical play until the liability franchise is built with new products (Smart Save, Freedom current accounts) and a TASC vertical, where the new LCR run-off of 40% is favourable.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan account numbers are falling and tonnage growth is weak. Is growth price-driven and what is the customer acquisition plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the account decline reflects the shift to tickets above Rs.10 lakh, with lower-risk LTVs and low tonnage since customers borrow only what they need. Target is gold at 30% of the book by 2030, including at least 5% gold-backed SME working capital. Management called the 53% YoY gold growth partly artificial due to the LAS reclassification.

qa_highlights.question: Retail asset growth timeline, fee income drivers, cost and CTI trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail growth to start from FY28; first focus is liabilities and cross-sell. No syndication fee in Q4 and PSLC premium was very low; core fees grew. Q4 cost rise was partly one-time CSR spend. CTI guided at 60-65% through FY27, with operating leverage from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is NIM bottoming and what drove yield compression?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM guided at 3.75-4%; Q4 was 3.83%. Management was unsure it has bottomed, citing business mix shifts. Yield compression came from repo cuts on BLG and MCLR repricing in wholesale, which management says has largely played out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL transition impact and how does it compare with existing provisions?
qa_highlights.answer: Based on the current IFRS model and December 2025 portfolio, the transition impact is described as not significant. Existing provisions (about Rs.105 crore Covid contingency and about Rs.210 crore buffer) may offset part of it, but the model is still being refreshed and a 1-2 month wait is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the SME slippage (10-11 accounts last quarter) resolved, and what are ROA/ROE levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give account-level detail; said some accounts were upgraded or recovered and some slippages were technical from migration-related MIS delays. ROA/ROE levers are cross-sell, gold book degrowth, and treasury gains from the AFS book; management guided RoA around 1.5% and RoE around 15% next year.

risks_watch: LCR and funding: heavy reliance on short-tenor bulk deposits (about 50% of term deposits) and low CASA (about 20%) raises cost and liquidity risk.
Gold concentration (about 53% of book) with prices and tonnage dependence; management says a further 10% price fall is not a concern.
Cost-to-income rising; CTI guided at 60-65% through FY27, with hiring and new cybersecurity advisory (April 27, 2026) spend uncertain.
SME and BLG growth stalled; West Asia crisis affects exports and supply chains.
Treasury and PSLC fee income volatile; Q4 had no MTM gain or syndication fee.
ECL transition model refresh still in progress; SMA-driven impact could be higher than estimated.
Retail asset growth not expected until FY28; the 25% loan growth target depends on deposit build-up.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality, ROA and ROE delivery, and the technology migration, but cautious and evasive on SME/BLG timing, ECL impact, the cybersecurity cost and whether NIM has bottomed. Management acknowledged that retail growth has been slow and has deferred meaningful retail asset growth to FY28.
key_quotes: As a bank, we are not here to build asset book first, but to build a franchise where liability comes first and assets follows.
I am confident that we are not shifting the goalposts from FY2030 to FY2032 or FY2033.
At this point, LCR is not our concern because we are significantly higher than these levels and NSFR is around 122%, which also gives comfort that we are on track on that front.
I never said that cost to income will come down from next quarter. I said it will remain for FY2027 in the range of 60 to 65%.

adds.what: Transaction banking systems (Vayana, Aurion Pro CMS, trade) going live
Dubai representative office (application extended; not yet live)

growth.why: Management targets loan growth around 25% in FY27, dependent on deposit and CASA build-up, while NIM, CTI and RoA/RoE are guided; with retail growth deferred to FY28 and no specific capacity or orders cited, backing is vague.
